author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty by address
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory, the paged page and the machine-readable document, accept an optional specialty name in the request address and list only veterinarians holding that specialty. The machine-readable form is reinstated as a supported capability (REQ-VET-004).
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-003] given /vets.html?specialty=<name>, when the page is opened, then only veterinarians holding that specialty are listed, with pagination applied to the narrowed list.
[REQ-VET-003] given /vets?specialty=<name>, when the JSON document is requested, then only veterinarians holding that specialty are returned.
[REQ-VET-003] given a name differing from a specialty's name only by letter case, when either surface is requested, then it matches that specialty.
[REQ-VET-003] given only the start of a specialty's name (a prefix), when either surface is requested, then no veterinarian is returned.
[REQ-VET-003] given a name no veterinarian's specialty matches, when either surface is requested, then HTTP 200 with the normal page or JSON document and an empty vet list.
[REQ-VET-003] given an empty or whitespace-only specialty value, when either surface is requested, then the response equals the request without the parameter.
[REQ-VET-003] given a narrowed HTML directory spanning more than one page, when its pagination links are rendered, then each link carries the specialty parameter.
[REQ-VET-003] given a veterinarian holding several specialties, when the directory is narrowed to one of them, then that veterinarian appears once and is shown with every specialty they hold.

[REQ-VET-004] given no specialty parameter, when /vets is requested, then every veterinarian is returned with their specialties, as today; /vets.html without the parameter is likewise unchanged (REQ-VET-001).
non_goals: Free-text or prefix search for veterinarians (NG-9 as narrowed); searching pets or visits (NG-9).
Any form, dropdown, or other page control for the filter on either surface; the owner deferred a visible control to a possible follow-up request.
Narrowing by more than one specialty in one request, or by any attribute other than specialty.
Paging the JSON document; it stays an unpaged list.
Reusing the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 id; it stays withdrawn.
notes: The PRD mints two IDs. REQ-VET-003 is the specialty filter on both surfaces, the slice's behavior. REQ-VET-004 reinstates the JSON /vets endpoint as a supported surface, per the owner's decision at intake line 1; its only new contract is that today's unfiltered behavior is now required. The slice ships both as one code-surface slice: the JSON half alone is 1-2 cycles and makes sense only alongside the HTML half. Non-goal ADR written: docs/adr/2026-10-24-non-goal-narrow-veterinarian-search.md. Its row in the docs/adr/README.md index is outside my write scope, so system-design-expert should add it. Open questions are recorded in the PRD, and the slice must not decide them as product behavior: whether a padded non-blank name (' radiology ') matches, and what a repeated specialty parameter returns. The narrowest reading normalizes only empty or whitespace-only values. Any trimming of padded values follows the system-design request-parameter normalization rule, and no test should assert product intent for it. The HTML page adds no new user-facing wording; an empty narrowed list reuses the existing page.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Existing vet feature package and patterns, small adjustments (system-design.md § Contracts rows VetRepository, VetController, Vets, CacheConfiguration now carry REQ-VET-003/REQ-VET-004; new § Scale and Load rows for the vet directory paths; the 'machine-readable route serves no requirement' Known Defects row removed, resolved by REQ-VET-004). VetRepository gains derived-query reads beside its findAll pair, the way OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith pages a derived query (grep basis: OwnerController.java:133-136, VetRepository.java; no IDE oracle connected). VetController binds an optional specialty request parameter on both routes; blank-to-absent is binding, not a business rule (architecture-principles § pattern catalog, Web controller row; testing-principles line 54 puts it at the web level). No service layer is introduced (feature-package ADR 2026-07-31; Open Question 2 stays open). Non-goal NG-9 as narrowed admits the slice (docs/adr/2026-10-24-non-goal-narrow-veterinarian-search.md); its index row is now in docs/adr/README.md.
integration_points: Repository: VetRepository gains two Spring Data derived reads for the distinct veterinarians whose specialty name equals the given name ignoring case, one paged (Pageable -> Page<Vet>) and one unpaged (Collection<Vet>), e.g. findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase. Derived queries only, no string-built JPQL (security-principles § Realization, injection row). The new reads carry @Transactional(readOnly = true) and NO @Cacheable (system-design § Scale and Load, Limits).

Binding, both routes: the specialty value binds as a request-scoped @RequestParam(required = false) String, never a persisted type. StringUtils.hasText false (null, empty, whitespace-only) -> the existing unfiltered findAll call, so the response equals the parameterless request. A non-blank value passes to the repository unchanged: no strip, no case folding in Java. A padded name or a repeated parameter is a PRD open question; no test asserts either.

HTML route /vets.html: the paged narrowed read feeds the existing addPaginationModel. The controller adds the normalized specialty (absent when blank) to the model. vetList.html builds every pagination href with Thymeleaf link-expression parameters, @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, never __${...}__ preprocessing or string concatenation of the specialty. Without a specialty, hrefs render without the parameter as today.
JSON route /vets: the unpaged narrowed read fills Vets.getVetList(); response shape unchanged; no match -> 200 with an empty vet list.
Double, framework transport: MockMvc in VetControllerTests (the sanctioned mock) for binding, blank-equals-absent, pagination-link carrying, JSON shaping, and HTTP 200 on no match.

Double, repository, in VetControllerTests: the existing @MockitoBean VetRepository stub, extended for the new reads. Reason: the @WebMvcTest slice has no data layer, and a hand-written double would re-implement the query semantics under test. The stub verifies only which read the controller selects and with what argument. It never stands in for match semantics.

Double, repository, match semantics: the real VetRepository on H2 seed data, in the existing @DataJpaTest ClinicServiceTests (or a sibling vet-package @DataJpaTest). It covers the whole name ignoring case, a prefix matching nothing, an unknown name yielding empty, and multi-specialty Linda Douglas (surgery + dentistry) appearing once with both specialties. It also checks that a vet with no specialty never appears and that page totals are counted over the narrowed list.

patterns.description: Paged derived-query search with request-parameter normalization before the repository call.
Existing addPaginationModel and Vets wrapper reused unchanged for the narrowed list.

risks.risk: Narrowed vet reads scale with data (system-design § Scale and Load, rows 'Veterinarians and their specialties', 'HTML vet directory', 'Serialized vet collection').
risks.mitigation: Database-side join filter with paging plus a count query for HTML. One unpaged query for JSON. Simplest readable form; the set is unrecorded, treated as bounded.

risks.risk: Caching narrowed reads would key the unbounded vets cache on caller-supplied specialty names, growing memory without limit (system-design § Scale and Load, Limits).
risks.mitigation: New reads carry no @Cacheable; only the existing unfiltered reads stay cached.

risks.risk: Duplicate rows: the inner join yields one row per matching specialty. specialties.name has no unique constraint, so case-variant duplicates would repeat a vet and inflate the page count (§ Scale and Load row 'Veterinarians and their specialties').
risks.mitigation: Distinct derived read (findDistinctBy...). Specialties stay loaded by the eager ManyToMany, not the filter join, so every specialty a vet holds is still shown.

risks.risk: Case-insensitive matching differs per vendor collation (system-design § Persistence; Known Defects, PostgreSQL owner search).
risks.mitigation: Use the IgnoreCase derived keyword, which upper-cases both sides in the query, independent of column collation. Do not rely on H2 or MySQL collation.

risks.risk: The specialty value is request-derived and reflected into pagination hrefs and the query (security-principles § Trust Boundaries, external input; § Realization, injection and XSS rows).
risks.mitigation: Bind it as a plain String, parameterized through the derived query, and render it only via Thymeleaf link-expression parameters, which URL-encode and escape. Never preprocess it with __${}__.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to judge. Design-doc writes this dispatch: docs/system-design.md (Contracts rows for REQ-VET-003/REQ-VET-004; new § Scale and Load section with three vet rows and the cache Limits bullet; Security Context inputs/outputs lines; removed the resolved machine-readable-route Known Defects row) and docs/adr/README.md (index row for the product expert's NG-9 non-goal ADR, as requested). No new ADR: no decision here constrains other slices beyond a current-state line. Brief gap for its owner: docs/security-principles.md § Realization has no row for resource exhaustion through caller-keyed caches or unbounded results. The Limits bullet in system-design carries the instance. The Open Question on vet cache invalidation (system-design § Open Questions 5) is unchanged; the narrowed reads are uncached, so it does not touch them.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The conditional `${specialty != null} ? @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})} : @{/vets.html(page=...)}` is repeated across five sibling pagination links (page numbers, first, previous, next, last). Each link carries the same two-branch href, so a change to the parameter contract needs five edits. The Control Flow checklist treats a conditional repeated across sibling sites in a template as duplication to compute once.
findings.fix: Compute the shared decision once, for example a `th:with` on the pagination container or a small fragment that takes the target page. Each link then references it, instead of repeating the ternary five times.

findings.description: The blank-versus-present decision `StringUtils.hasText(specialty)` is made in three places: showVetList (to set the model attribute), findPaginated, and showResourcesVetList. In the HTML route the same normalization runs twice per request, in two methods, and the model attribute and the query must stay in agreement. A later edit to one site can make the page links and the query disagree. In the JSON route the inline ternary inside `addAll(...)` also mixes the choice of read with the filling of the list, which reads harder than the original one-liner.
findings.fix: Normalize once per handler, for example `String activeSpecialty = StringUtils.hasText(specialty) ? specialty : null;`, and pass that value on. Use it for both the model attribute and the repository selection. In the JSON handler, pull the read selection out into a named local or private method before `addAll`.

Workload fit: database-side distinct join with paging and a count query for HTML, and one unpaged query for JSON, as the Scale and Load rows record (docs/system-design.md:126-128). New reads carry no @Cacheable, in line with the Limits bullet at line 131.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the request-derived `specialty` reaches the database only through the Spring Data derived queries `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String specialtyName, Pageable pageable)` and `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String specialtyName)` (VetRepository.java diff), which bind it as a parameter. A grep of the diff's added lines for `@Query|createQuery|nativeQuery` returned only one prose line in docs/system-design.md, so no query text is built by string concatenation.

XSS and template-expression injection: in vetList.html, lines 30-50 put `specialty` only inside Thymeleaf link-expression parameters, e.g. line 30 `@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}`. Thymeleaf URL-encodes these parameters. The change also removes the old `__${...}__` preprocessing from the pagination hrefs, e.g. `@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}`, so the template has less preprocessing than before. The added-line grep for `__${|utext` found no new preprocessing or unescaped output. Elsewhere `specialty` appears only as the `th:each` loop variable at line 20, `th:each="specialty : ${vet.specialties}"`, which is rendered through `th:text`.

Cache poisoning and unbounded cache growth: the new caller-keyed finders are deliberately left uncached, as the Javadoc says. `grep -F '@Cacheable'` on VetRepository.java matches only the two pre-existing `findAll` methods at lines 45 and 55, `@Cacheable("vets")`, so an attacker cannot grow the `vets` cache or put a narrowed result into the unfiltered key.

Mass assignment and request binding: the new input is a scalar `@RequestParam(required = false) String specialty` on both `/vets.html` and `/vets`, not a bound domain object. No `@ModelAttribute` or `@RequestBody` target is added.

Exposed surface: no new route is added. Both existing read-only GET routes gain an optional filter that returns a subset of data already public on the same routes, so nothing is exposed beyond the documented demonstration baseline (docs/security-principles.md, 'Widening the exposed surface' row). A blank value falls back to the unfiltered path via `StringUtils.hasText`, and an unmatched name returns an empty list rather than an error, so no exception message reaches the error page.

Secrets: a grep of the diff's added lines for `password|token|secret|apikey|api_key|credential` matched only the prose 'Environment variables supplying the datasource credentials' in docs/system-design.md. No credential is added.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set, so no dependency changed. `grep -F -i dependencycheck build.gradle` returned nothing, so OWASP Dependency-Check is not configured and no NVD match ran in this review. `./gradlew dependencies` (runtimeClasspath) resolves Spring Boot 4.1.1, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE (thymeleaf-spring6 3.1.5.RELEASE) and Jackson databind 3.1.5 (tools.jackson.core). `./gradlew test` was not run by this reviewer; the build-pass record (line 7) lists the gate's test run.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Fix-delta scope: reviewed `python3 scripts/changeset.py --base-tree e974c577836c8abc1a1f139cd972673341967dcd` (the review-plan's basis.prev_tree_sha). The private finders branch on `specialty != null`, so a blank value still falls back to the unfiltered path. Secrets and supply chain: the delta's added lines contain no credential-like literal (checked by reading the full delta above). build.gradle is not in the change set, so no dependency changed. Dependency-Check is not configured, so no NVD match ran. The resolved versions in my round-1 record (line 16: Spring Boot 4.1.1, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, Jackson databind 3.1.5) are unchanged. `./gradlew test` was not run by this reviewer; the build-pass at line 20 lists the gate's test run.
